top_stories.title: Anthropic launches Claude Opus 5.5, undercutting OpenAI on price and performance
points: Opus 5.5 scores 58 on Anthropic's Intelligence Index, topping previous leaders Fable 5.1 and GPT-6 Astra (both at 53).
Matches Fable-level performance while costing 40% less than the previous Opus 5 model, with extra savings from token caching (reusing previously computed sequences within 30 minutes to cut costs).
Addresses widely criticized unnatural 'Claudish' writing style, producing more natural text across applications.
Achieved its best-ever score on internal alignment/safety benchmarking (a measure of how well an AI follows intended values), the first release under Anthropic's stated 'pacing' commitment.
Paid plans get expanded five-hour usage limits plus an on-demand rate-limit reset feature to encourage adoption.

unique_angles.point: Released just 90 minutes before OpenAI's competing GPT-6 launch, intensifying the industry's release-day rivalry.

top_stories.title: OpenAI launches GPT-6 Sol and Luna at half the price
points: Two new models: GPT-6 Sol for advanced reasoning/complex problem-solving, GPT-6 Luna optimized for speed and everyday tasks.
API pricing cut roughly 50% (Luna at $0.10/$0.50 per million tokens, Sol at $2/$10), while performance improves only slightly.
Extends advanced coding, factuality, and computer-use (AI interacting with software interfaces like a human would) capabilities down to cheaper tiers.
Rolling out immediately across ChatGPT Work, Codex, and most subscription tiers, with banked usage-limit resets mirroring Anthropic's competitive moves.

unique_angles.point: Sam Altman said the industry's 'pacing era' 'does not mean stopping,' framing continued rapid releases despite safety calls.

items.title: OpenAI taps mathematicians to review AI math breakthroughs
points: OpenAI's internal math model has resolved 100+ open problems across most branches of mathematics since August 28, including a claimed resolution of Navier–Stokes (a centuries-unsolved fundamental fluid dynamics equation).

Nine top mathematicians, including Fields Medalists Timothy Gowers and Martin Hairer, now advise via Princeton's Institute for Advanced Study to vet results for correctness, originality, and credit—but cannot control the model's output pace.
Move responds to a letter from 27 Fields Medalists accusing AI labs of rushing unreviewed results, though the new process doesn't actually slow releases.

items.title: a16z launches $42M AI-era college alternative
points: Andreessen Horowitz's 'Horowitz Andreessen Academy' is a one-year, $42M program for recent high school grads starting Fall 2027, replacing degrees with startup projects and industry mentorship (including Sam Altman).
Admissions judge what applicants have built rather than grades/test scores; founding class capped at ~50 students.
Students get $50,000 in compute credits, $5,000 travel budgets, and startup internships, with no homework or exams; a pricier two-year version is planned for 2028 pending regulatory approval.

items.title: OpenAI and Sam Altman sued over Tumbler Ridge shooting
points: British Columbia alleges OpenAI and Sam Altman failed to alert police after the Tumbler Ridge shooter's flagged ChatGPT usage.

items.title: Alibaba unveils next-gen AI chip and massive scaling plans
points: New chip delivers 3x performance gains over its predecessor.
Alibaba plans 5–10 trillion parameter models and 20 gigawatts of data-center capacity by 2032.

items.title: Mirage ships Tesseract, an AI video-editing suite for agents
points: Lets AI agents work directly with video editing tools—compositions, keyframes, audio—to create and refine video assets.

items.title: AI agent security: isolating OAuth tokens from agents
points: Agents reading malicious documents can be tricked into following hidden instructions; if they hold a user's OAuth token (an access credential for connected apps/APIs), this can turn into full account takeover via prompt injection.
WorkOS Relay keeps credentials on WorkOS servers, attaching them only to pre-approved requests sent to allow-listed servers, so the agent itself never sees the token.

items.title: Grok Bot automates new-hire onboarding
points: Connects to Google Drive, Notion, SharePoint, Outlook, and Teams to pull handbooks, checklists, and IT guides automatically.
Given just a hire's name, role, and start date, it builds a first-week checklist and answers questions only from approved company sources.
Can be tested, corrected, and saved as a reusable 'Skill' for standardizing onboarding across future hires.

items.title: SWE-Bench Pro V2 reveals harder, more realistic coding benchmark
points: New benchmark includes 642 real-world software engineering tasks drawn from 11 code repositories, fixing errors present in earlier versions.
Top models, including GPT-6 and Claude Opus 4.1, score only about 23%, sharply lower than on previous benchmarks, reflecting realistic multi-file coding complexity.

items.title: AI leaders to address UN Security Council on safety
points: Sam Altman (OpenAI) and Dario Amodei (Anthropic) are expected to speak to the UN Security Council about AI safety and regulation amid rising concerns over AI risks.

items.title: AI safety and infrastructure advances
points: Google published RRSI, a method for self-improving AI agents that reduces benchmark overfitting (over-tuning to specific test cases) while improving real-world performance across eight benchmarks using fewer policy tokens (decision outputs).
vLLM introduced hardware-agnostic layers supporting diverse GPU types while retaining 96.6% of the efficiency of native implementations on premium hardware.

New memory optimization techniques bound four major bottlenecks in training large Mixture-of-Experts models (architectures that split computation across specialized sub-models) without sacrificing calculation accuracy.

items.title: China and biotech AI infrastructure developments
points: China's ChangXin Memory Technologies claims parity with Samsung and Micron, with a new DRAM platform yielding 50% more chips per wafer and 50% higher capacity than its prior generation.

The Biological Computing Co. partnered with AWS to commercialize neuron-derived AI video models, porting insights from lab-grown neurons into software that runs on standard cloud GPUs without biological hardware.

sections.title: 1. Anthropic's Opus 5.5 Shifts Model Competition

sections.title: 3. AI Agent Security: OAuth Token Isolation

WorkOS Relay solution keeps credentials on WorkOS servers, attaches them only to approved requests, sends only to allow-listed servers—agent never sees the token itself.
Prevents agents from accidentally or maliciously abusing user permissions without degrading their ability to perform authorized tasks.
